dataset.algorithm:
Premeasurement panel selection; standard library only, no model imports.

Algorithm v1: scene quotas use constrained Hamilton apportionment. Fix scenes
whose proportional ideal is below the minimum at that minimum, recompute ideals
on the remaining population, floor ideals, then give remaining seats in descending
fractional-remainder order (lexicographic scene key breaks ties). Capacity is never
exceeded. Within each scene, apportion its quota proportionally over the population's
three GLOBAL rank tertiles. Rank by (continuous GT length, string episode ID),
assign tertile min(2, floor(3*rank/N)); equal lengths may cross a boundary, with
lexicographic episode IDs breaking ties. No model outputs inform these choices.

Selection: separate random.Random(seed) streams for shared, D-e and determinism
panels; canonical sorted scene/stratum/ID order before shuffle. Within each fixed
shared-panel stratum shuffle >=34-action and shorter candidates separately, then
take long candidates first. D-e has scene quotas only and no length preference.
The 60 determinism episodes are scene-proportional within the selected 600.
Action count includes terminal STOP; continuous path length is the sum of 3D
Euclidean distances between successive GT locations, not reference-path length
or action count. Missing/malformed GT fails closed instead of silently excluding
episodes. Missing instruction_id defaults to episode_id (VLN-CE convention).

# User-authorized scope update

The user instructed: “Skip it, remove the D-g”.

The active study consists of D-a through D-f and the original R1–R5 decision table. D-g gradient measurements, its 32-episode subset, gradient tests, figures, and recovery-checkpoint requirements are removed. D-e no longer depends on D-g completion. No objective-interference conclusion will be reported.

TASK_SPEC.md remains the unchanged original specification for provenance; this later user instruction overrides its D-g requirements. All remaining parity gates, diagnostic definitions, tolerances, no-training constraints, and deliverables remain in force. Trained-head readouts in D-a/D-b remain optional under the original specification; their absence does not block the study. D-f may use dummy heads only after its specified invariance gate passes.

## Dataset confirmation after rendering failure

After receiving the failed rendering-gate report, the user confirmed the R2R training data as XinyuYan/JanusVLN_Trajectory_Data and the RxR data as the supplied 15-degree version, and instructed: “Just use them for me”. This is interpreted as authorization to proceed with these specified datasets despite the recorded rendering discrepancy. The original failed result remains intact and must be disclosed as a limitation; it is not relabeled passed and its tolerance is not changed. The model parity gates and R1–R5 definitions remain unchanged. Prefer existing archive val_unseen images when available; otherwise retain the prescribed evaluation renderer and explicitly report the unmatched training-image condition. No substitution of training episodes for the frozen val_unseen panel is authorized.
# Approved decision-token KL

The user explicitly selected “Use decision-token KL (recommended)”. D-b reports KL(original || ablated) over the full vocabulary at teacher-forced response decision positions, in nats. These generative exports do not have a four-semantic-action output head. No invented four-action normalization is used. Recall and ablation primary contrasts are unchanged.
